papers.title_in_file: On quantum ensembles of quantum classifiers
papers.what_it_is: A short preprint that shows the accuracy-weighted quantum ensemble of quantum classifiers can be dequantised via rejection sampling, and that the general quantum ensemble framework contains the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm.

existing.note: Confirmed. The body also limits what is meant: the accuracy-weighted scheme is translated to rejection sampling, and other weighing schemes may not translate.
existing.value: The authors state that the accuracy-weighted quantum ensemble, a specific implementation of the quantum ensemble of quantum classifiers, can be fully dequantised.
quotes: we demonstrate that a speciﬁc implementation of the quantum ensemble of quantum classiﬁers, called the accuracy-weighted quantum ensemble, can be fully dequantised.
weighing scheme may be translated to a classical algorithm, namely, rejection sampling
existing.certainty_reason: Abstract states it; the dequantising section gives the argument (postselection mirrors the rejection decision of rejection sampling).

existing.note: Confirmed. The text layer places the Conclusion before the page-5 marker, so the page anchor is p.4 rather than p.5.
existing.value: The authors state that the Deutsch-Jozsa reduction does not necessarily represent a quantum ensemble that is useful for machine learning.
quotes: This Deutsch-Jozsa reduction, however, does not necessarily represent a quantum ensemble that is useful for machine learning.
existing.certainty_reason: Conclusion states it as the limit of the reduction.

assertions.value: The authors describe the quantum ensemble of quantum classifiers as an exponentially large ensemble of quantum classifiers computed in parallel, weighed by a specified weighing scheme, with the collective prediction obtained through a single qubit measurement.
assertions.anchor: Introduction, p.1
quotes: An exponentially large ensemble of quantum classiﬁers are computed in parallel, weighed according to a speciﬁed weighing scheme and their collective prediction is obtained through a single qubit measurement.
assertions.certainty_reason: Introduction describes the framework under study (attributed to the earlier work it reviews).

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantum ensemble of quantum classifiers is intended to be executed end-to-end on a quantum device, and designed to harness the properties of quantum computing.
assertions.anchor: Introduction, p.1
quotes: is intended to be executed end-toend on a quantum device and designed to harness the properties of quantum computing
assertions.certainty_reason: Introduction states the intended execution model.

assertions.value: The authors state that a good first step in analysing claims such as exponential speed ups for a quantum machine learning algorithm is to check whether it can be efficiently replicated on a classical computer.
assertions.anchor: Introduction, p.1
quotes: A good ﬁrst step in analysing the validity of these claims is to check if the quantum machine learning algorithm can be eﬃciently replicated on a classical computer.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper shows the accuracy-weighted scheme efficiently translates to a classical algorithm, while the general quantum ensemble framework is proven to contain the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm and so can compute a classically hard problem where quantum computing may offer an advantage.
assertions.anchor: Introduction, pp.1-2
quotes: whilst the general quantum ensemble framework is proven to contain the DeutschJozsa algorithm and thus has the ability to compute a classically hard problem where quantum computing may oﬀer an advantage [16, 17].
assertions.certainty_reason: Introduction states the two results of the paper.

assertions.value: The authors define rejection sampling as a way to sample from a distribution that is difficult to sample from but whose point evaluations are possible, by drawing from an easy-to-sample distribution scaled by a finite factor.
assertions.anchor: Dequantising the accuracy-weighted scheme, p.2
quotes: Rejection sampling allows one to sample from a distribution p(x) that is diﬃcult to sample from, but point evaluations for a given x are possible.
assertions.certainty_reason: Definition given in the section.

assertions.value: The authors define the Deutsch-Jozsa problem: a function g guaranteed to be either constant or balanced, with the goal of determining which.
assertions.anchor: Linking the Deutsch-Jozsa and quantum ensemble frameworks, p.3
quotes: where g is guaranteed to be either constant (all zeros or all ones) or balanced (half zeros and half ones).
The goal is to determine if g is constant or balanced.

assertions.value: The authors state that a classical computer would need at worst 2n/2 + 1 queries of the function g (the text layer prints the exponent flat, read as two to the power of n over two, plus one), while the Deutsch-Jozsa protocol on a quantum computer reaches the goal with certainty in just one measurement.
assertions.anchor: Linking the Deutsch-Jozsa and quantum ensemble frameworks, p.3
quotes: This would take a classical computer at worst 2n/2 + 1 queries of the function g, but using the DeutschJozsa protocol on a quantum computer, one may achieve the goal with certainty in just one measurement [26].

assertions.value: The authors state that the probability of measuring the all-zero state at the end of the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm is equal to 1 if g is constant and 0 if g is balanced.
assertions.anchor: Linking the Deutsch-Jozsa and quantum ensemble frameworks, step v, p.3
quotes: which is equal to 1 if g(x) is constant and 0 if g(x) is balanced.

assertions.value: The authors state that the q-ensemble framework can be shown to contain the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm if W is chosen to implement uniform weights and A = (H⊗n ⊗ I) Ug (I⊗n ⊗ X) (I⊗n ⊗ H), where Ug is a unitary implementing the function g.
assertions.anchor: Linking the Deutsch-Jozsa and quantum ensemble frameworks, p.3
quotes: the q-ensemble framework can be shown to contain the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm if we choose W from Equation (3) to implement uniform weights and let A = (H⊗n ⊗ I) Ug (I⊗n ⊗ X) (I⊗n ⊗ H) where Ug is again a unitary implementing the function g.
assertions.certainty_reason: The statement and its conditions (uniform weights, the stated form of A) are quoted from the section that proves it.

assertions.value: The authors state that the probability of measuring the output qubit in state zero in the embedded circuit is the sum of the weights over the models with prediction +1, normalised by a factor, which corresponds to a prediction of -1 for the q-ensemble.

assertions.value: The authors state that, through congruence of steps i. to v. with steps 1. to 5., they have demonstrated that the q-ensemble contains a classically hard computation that is amenable to a quantum advantage.
assertions.anchor: Linking the Deutsch-Jozsa and quantum ensemble frameworks, p.4

assertions.reader_inference: The demonstration is a step-by-step matching of circuits, not a numbered theorem; the construction uses uniform weights and an empty data register, so no data are learned.
